editorial:
Imagine having a brother who shares your passion for dance, but you both choose completely opposite paths in life. You get to see this play out in Communist Hungary, where one brother runs away to the West to make money and the other stays behind to climb the ranks of the government party. It is a story about how power, money, and politics can rip a family apart. The vibe is heavy and emotional, focusing on the tension between two people who used to be close but now barely recognize each other. When they finally reunite after twenty years, you can feel the bitterness and regret in every scene.

The acting is the best part here because the dancers really sell the pain and anger through their movements. While the story moves a bit slow at times, the payoff is worth it for anyone who likes deep family dramas.
endingExplained: The movie ends with a final, intense dance that acts as a conversation they could not have with words. You see the two brothers finally face the truth about their choices and the damage they caused. Instead of a happy reunion, the ending feels more like a sad release. They realize that while they are still brothers, the time they lost can never be recovered, leaving them both broken and alone in the end.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about family conflict and the arts.
